title: Scrutiny of v_c regressors: form is lossy (rank), going is a blind spot
author: modelling
summary: Audit of effective-v_c terms. (1) FORM is the dominant signal but coupled through a CENSORED rank proxy (relative-finish): winning by a nose vs 10 lengths both give pos=1, discarding the margin = the …
text: scrutiny of v_c regressors: form is lossy (rank), going is a blind spot scrutiny form speed-figure going critical-power methodology v_c audit of effective-v_c terms. (1) form is the dominant signal but coupled through a censored rank proxy (relative-finish): winning by a nose vs 10 lengths both give pos=1, discarding the margin = the velocity info. mechanistic upgrade: a speed figure from lbw (lengths behind winner) + finishtime -> velocity deficit in m/s, coefficient ~1 (kinematic), normalised to a going/distance/class par. data available in results_rich. highest-value, cleanest. (2) going is a real v_c modifier (soft ground raises locomotion cost, differentially by horse) that the residual diagnosis cannot see -- it's a race-level constant that vanishes under within-race renormalisation. systematic blind spot of the whole loop; needs a calibration-by-going instrument, not the residual regression. (3) v_c estimator is a one-race min-velocity heuristic; principled version is the critical-power hyperbola d=v_c*t+w' across multi-distance runs. (4) jockey is reduced-form + selection-confounded; a clean coupling would route it through trip geometry/policy not raw v_c -- leave for now. rating is well-incorporated (resid ~0). meta: the residual instrument is blind to race-level physics (going/distance/class/track) by construction -- it will keep finding within-race mechanisms and miss condition mechanisms.

title: Full power-balance EOM underperforms kinematic by ~1.4 nats/race (win-prob)
author: modelling
summary: Tried the most-fundamental mass coupling: run the power-balance EOM (hkjc.model.eom) in production so declared mass enters every term via Newton's law, with one allometric constant b. Built dynamics.w…
text: full power-balance eom underperforms kinematic by ~1.4 nats/race (win-prob) eom mass allometric negative-result physics-migration steady-state tried the most-fundamental mass coupling: run the power-balance eom (hkjc.model.eom) in production so declared mass enters every term via newton's law, with one allometric constant b. built dynamics.win_probs + a sim='eom' path in fit.py (kinematic-calibrated gains form_gain=4, w_prime_gain=2). result on a 42-race slice: eom winner-logp -3.68 to -4.38 vs kinematic -2.30. removing drag (cda=0) recovers only ~0.7; lowering tau/noise doesn't help. the eom's dynamics (accel phase, w'-depletion fade, power smoothing) compress the ability spread the kinematic sim preserves. key insight: the (m/m_field)^(b-1) v_c factor is not an arbitrary tack-on -- it is the eom's exact steady-state solution (v_c=p_c/(k_loco*m*g), p_c=k*m^b). it captures the win-determining mass->v_c physics at kinematic accuracy; the full integrated eom only adds second-order transients that are currently mis-calibrated and hurt. making the full eom competitive needs a from-scratch recalibration (gains up, noise down, fade/drag retuned) starting 1.4 nats behind, uncertain it matches. recommendation: bake the steady-state allometric law (first-principles, ready now); treat the full dynamic-eom migration as a separate greenlit project.

text: mass coupling parked -- real residual but low-leverage (b=1 isometric optimal) mass allometric parsimony low-leverage negative-result calibrated the steady-state allometric law v_c*(m/m_field)^(b-1) on the quick backtest. b=1.0 (no mass effect) is optimal; b=1.5->47%, b=2->-9%, monotone worse. fine check: b=1.05/1.10 also worse than 1.0. so despite the confirmed-real bodywt residual (t=+8.8, survives rating+class), coupling mass to v_c does not improve goodness-of-fit -- it is low-leverage on the winner's prob, the same lesson as draw. physical reading: b~1 = isometric (aerobic power and carrying-cost both scale ~linearly with mass, cancelling) => no net v_c effect. per parsimony (physics-plausible + real-residual is not sufficient; it must move the needle), mass is left out. the high-leverage lever remains w' (+1.4pp). eom/allometric_b/dynamics.win_probs kept as inert recorded infrastructure (default b=1). next: speed-figure form (velocity vs rank).

title: Noise framing resolved: velocity-mult (=log-normal proportional time-noise) wins; statistical model can't do interactions
author: modelling
summary: Tested finishing-time noise per the standard-theory reframing. FULL-SCALE: velocity-multiplicative constant sigma_v = 48.3% (best). Finishing-TIME ADDITIVE: Gumbel->Plackett-Luce closed form peaks 46.…
text: noise framing resolved: velocity-mult (=log-normal proportional time-noise) wins; statistical model can't do interactions noise-model finishing-time plackett-luce interactions architecture parsimony tested finishing-time noise per the standard-theory reframing. full-scale: velocity-multiplicative constant sigma_v = 48.3% (best). finishing-time additive: gumbel->plackett-luce closed form peaks 46.4% @sigma_t=5s; gaussian->probit 44.9% @8s -- both slightly worse. distance-dependent noise: exp=0 (flat) best; exp=0.5 (the diffusion/first-passage sqrt(d) law) 47.7%, worse -- so the calibration-by-condition distance gradient was small-sample/awt noise, not robust. parsimony: keep sigma_v flat. reconciliation: constant-sigma_v velocity model is a finishing-time model -- log-normal noise proportional to time (sigma_t ∝ mu), the standard model for positive performance quantities; data prefers proportional over additive. key caveat (user): the purely statistical framework (probit/pl/softmax) cannot mechanistically model interactions -- blocking, real-time tactics, jockey policy. that is the agent-based sim's reason to exist (the physics+game-theory core). corrected architecture conclusion: probit = fast dev surrogate for the win-calibration loop (35x, matches because interactions are low-leverage for win); the agent-based sim stays as the production substrate for interactions/policy/exotics. not a replacement. pl/time/probit kept as documented fit.py modes. noise + statistical-reformulation levers exhausted. remaining concrete lever: awt 1650m badly miscalibrated (13%).

title: FUTURE DIRECTION: stat-mech / condensed-matter machinery for the interaction layer
author: modelling
summary: User idea (later, not now). The race is a driven, interacting, non-equilibrium many-body system; condensed-matter / stat-mech gives the right tools to go from MICRO interactions to MACRO finishing-ord…
text:
future direction: stat-mech / condensed-matter machinery for the interaction layer future-direction stat-mech condensed-matter interactions mean-field-games tasep plackett-luce game-theory user idea (later, not now). the race is a driven, interacting, non-equilibrium many-body system; condensed-matter / stat-mech gives the right tools to go from micro interactions to macro finishing-order observables, potentially semi-analytically (vs brute-force monte-carlo). concrete mappings to explore:
- blocking -> exclusion processes (tasep / multi-lane asep): the car-following 'can't pass through' is hard-core exclusion -- the canonical solved model for traffic; gives current-density relations, jamming, and correlation functions analytically.
- drafting -> active matter / self-propelled particles with wake-attraction (peloton dynamics).
- jockey policy / tactics -> mean-field games (lasry-lions): the continuum limit of n agents optimising pace/position simultaneously = coupled hjb (optimal control) + fokker-planck (density). this is the rigorous mathematical home for the project's physics(plant)+game-theory(policy) thesis -- the 'best-response pace layer' is a mean-field game.
- quenched disorder (abilities) -> replica/cavity for the outcome distribution over ability disorder.
unifying picture: plackett-luce is the free (non-interacting) theory -- independent finishing times. interactions (exclusion/drafting/tactics) are couplings on top => an 'interacting plackett-luce' / effective field theory whose observables are the finishing-order probabilities; the agent-based sim is its monte-carlo, stat-mech could give analytic/perturbative (cluster/virial-expansion) results. this bridges the fast statistical model (free theory, great for win) and the interaction modelling (perturbations, matters for place/exotics/policy).

title: Diffusion law (Inverse-Gaussian first-passage) tested: ties the in-place log-normal noise
author: modelling
summary: Per the diffusion-law correction: finishing time = first-passage of dx=v·dt+sqrt(2D)·dW => INVERSE GAUSSIAN (Wald), strictly positive, Var(T)=2D·L/v^3. Implemented sim='wald' (one physical param, diff…
text: diffusion law (inverse-gaussian first-passage) tested: ties the in-place log-normal noise diffusion inverse-gaussian wald first-passage noise-model unification foundation per the diffusion-law correction: finishing time = first-passage of dx=v·dt+sqrt(2d)·dw => inverse gaussian (wald), strictly positive, var(t)=2d·l/v^3. implemented sim='wald' (one physical param, diffusion coef d). full-scale sweep: peaks d~160-180 -> 47.7%, vs velocity-multiplicative (=log-normal time) 48.2% -- a tie within noise. both are correct positive-time models, both one numpy call (equal efficiency); fit marginally favors the log-normal already in place. conclusion: the noise foundation is validated -- the principled diffusion law agrees with the in-place model to ~0.5pp, so adopting the diffusion framing later (for interactions) costs nothing. unifying picture: each horse = drift-diffusion particle (drift=ability, diffusion=d). non-interacting limit = independent inverse-gaussian finishing times (the fast win surrogate). with interactions (exclusion=blocking/tasep, coupling=drafting, policy=mean-field game) = the agent-based sim is the monte-carlo of the same many-body drift-diffusion. so the fast surrogate and the interacting sim are one model at different interaction orders -- the substrate for the stat-mech program. keep log-normal noise for now (marginally better, in place); diffusion is the principled foundation for the interaction layer. fit.py keeps probit/pl/time/wald as documented modes.

title: AWT fix in the diffusion framework: D_awt = 2x D_turf (no ad-hoc velocity knob)
author: modelling
summary: AWT (1650m) was 13% of market (over-confident + weak ability transfer). FIRST attempt used an ad-hoc multiplier on velocity speed_noise -- wrong framework (user). CORRECT: in the diffusion (Wald) mode…
text: awt fix in the diffusion framework: d_awt = 2x d_turf (no ad-hoc velocity knob) awt diffusion surface noise-model ability-transfer calibration awt (1650m) was 13% of market (over-confident + weak ability transfer). first attempt used an ad-hoc multiplier on velocity speed_noise -- wrong framework (user). correct: in the diffusion (wald) model the noise is the diffusion coefficient d; awt is simply a more diffusive surface (kickback, less reliable turf-trained signal) => larger d. calibrated (wald, d_turf=170): awt d = 2x turf d is optimal -> awt 16.7%->23.7% (vs 12.7% velocity baseline), overall 47.4->47.7%, turf unchanged 48.8%. a clean physical statement (awt 2x as diffusive), one surface-dependent physical parameter, not a tuned velocity knob. remaining: awt 23.7% << turf 48.8% is the genuine ability-transfer weakness (model ranks awt winners at percentile 0.59 vs 0.70 turf) -- the turf-dominated form/v_c doesn't apply to all-weather; surface-specific ability is the fix but data-starved (awt ~6% of races). timing: wald sampling 1.6x probit (inv-gaussian vs gaussian), both ~30-40s full-scale; closed-form pl is ~2000x faster (no sampling) -- the instant proxy for sweeps. architecture: this is the case for adopting diffusion as the noise model (physical, condition-dependence is real, interaction-ready); ~0.5pp turf cost vs velocity-mult. eventually the agent-based sim's integrator should use per-timestep sqrt(2d)dw (non-interacting limit = wald).

text: breakthrough: recency-weighted form (half-life ~2 races) lifts st 48% -> 56% of market (+7.8pp) recency form breakthrough ability shrinkage knob-scan knob scan found the biggest lever of the session. replacing the career expanding-mean form with an exp-weighted (recency) form, half-life ~2 races: career 48.1% -> recency 55.9%. half-life sweep is a clean smooth interior optimum (0.7->49.4, 1.0->53.4, 1.5->55.6, 2.0->55.9, 3.0->55.2, 5.0->53.6, 10->51.4, career->48.1) -- the signature of real signal. leak-verified: recency_form_table uses ewm_mean().shift(1).over(horse_id), strictly prior (first run null); manually confirmed prior-only. this overturns the old 'recency doesn't transfer to the abm' finding (that was the stale form_gain=2 abm). mechanism: career-average form is stale over hk's long careers (horses improve/decline, change class); recency tracks current ability and aligns with how the market weights recent runs -> big %market jump. action: make recency form (hl~2) the production form; re-calibrate form_gain and re-confirm w_prime_gain/jockey_gain/shrink_mult under it (the form spread changed). also found this scan: eb shrink_mult on the sectional v_c residual is over-trusted -- 0.5 (48.8%) and even 0.0 (48.5%) beat 1.0 (48.1%); the sectional energetics barely earns its keep for win. trainer parked (+0.2pp, redundant with jockey+rating).

title: Model lineup: drop probit (velocity-mult); Wald (diffusion) is production, PL the fast probe
author: modelling
summary: Per the first-principles mindframe, dropped the probit (velocity-multiplicative) win model -- an odd in-between: noise on velocity not the physical finishing-time observable, and a one-shot draw not a…
text: model lineup: drop probit (velocity-mult); wald (diffusion) is production, pl the fast probe wald diffusion probit plackett-luce model-lineup jax n_samples first-principles per the first-principles mindframe, dropped the probit (velocity-multiplicative) win model -- an odd in-between: noise on velocity not the physical finishing-time observable, and a one-shot draw not a diffusion. also dropped the additive-gaussian 'time' mode (allows t<0). lineup now: sim='wald' (default, the production win model -- drift-diffusion first-passage / inverse-gaussian, the principled noise law, one physical d, surface-dependent awt 2x, ~55.5% of market); sim='pl' (closed-form plackett-luce, instant, the fast-and-dirty probe); sim='kinematic' (jax traffic sim, for interactions/exotics only -- traffic low-leverage for win); sim='eom' (inert infra). wald speedup (user asked, jax available): jax only 1.2x on cpu (no gpu; the ig sampling is memory-bound; a single batched (races,ns,n) call is worse, 195s). the real quick win is n_samples: 4000->55.3%, 8000->55.5%, 20000->55.5% -- ~3x faster at 4k for <0.2pp. production n_samples=6000 already fine. further option (not done): the ig is near-gaussian here (mu/lam~0.02), so a sampling-free gaussian-approx probit with the diffusion variance could be ~instant -- an approximation to verify. studies repointed probit->wald; model_state + sim constant updated.

title: Re-diagnosis at the recency (56%) baseline rebalanced the ability gains: FORM_GAIN 4->5, W_PRIME_GAIN 2->1
author: modelling
summary: The recency-form switch changed the residual regime, so the gains baked for CAREER form went stale. Fresh market-residual diagnosis (SIM=wald): form flipped to UNDER-weighted (t=+11.4 at FG=4) because…
text: re-diagnosis at the recency (56%) baseline rebalanced the ability gains: form_gain 4->5, w_prime_gain 2->1 recalibration form-gain w-prime-gain re-diagnosis recency wald parsimony the recency-form switch changed the residual regime, so the gains baked for career form went stale. fresh market-residual diagnosis (sim=wald): form flipped to under-weighted (t=+11.4 at fg=4) because recency form is a sharper, higher-variance signal than the career mean; w_prime flipped to over-weighted (t=-8.95) because recency form absorbed the reserve signal. recalibrated: form_gain 4->5 (clean interior optimum, +0.9pp full scale; 6-7 fall off a cliff); w_prime_gain 2->1 (win-prob impact flat over 0-2 -- w' is a finishing-margin effect, low-leverage on who wins -- so parsimony + the residual sign both say revert the amplification we added in the career era). diff_coef d=170 already optimal (sharper hurts, so v_c_eb's under-trust is not a global-confidence problem). re-diagnosis confirms: form neutralised (->-8.7, the fg optimum edge), v_c_eb +14.5->-4.0, w_prime ->+1.4. method note: speed_noise is a no-op under wald (wald uses diff_coef, not speed_noise) -- don't sweep it for the production model. also fixed quick_eval determinism: polars unique() is not order-stable, so the test_cap subsample jittered ~1.7pp run-to-run; sorted the ids.

title: BREAKTHROUGH: re-added bend ground-loss to the wald drift (DRAW_GAIN=0.003) -> ST 56->58% of market
author: modelling
summary: The #1 residual at 56% was draw (t=-26.5). ROOT CAUSE: production wald (and pl) had NO draw term at all -- draw/bend_curvature lived ONLY in the kinematic geometry sim, and was silently DROPPED when w…
text: breakthrough: re-added bend ground-loss to the wald drift (draw_gain=0.003) -> st 56->58% of market draw bend-ground-loss wald breakthrough interaction abm re-diagnosis first-principles the #1 residual at 56% was draw (t=-26.5). root cause: production wald (and pl) had no draw term at all -- draw/bend_curvature lived only in the kinematic geometry sim, and was silently dropped when wald became production. (the naive 'over-weights' label was wrong: the model had zero draw signal while the market prices the inside-draw advantage.) fix (physics, not a regressor): a horse drawn k lanes off the rail runs a longer arc round the turns -> larger effective distance -> longer first-passage time. l_eff = dist*(1+draw_gain*(draw-1)) in the wald/pl drift. geometry fixes the sign; the magnitude is calibrated and absorbs jockeys steering toward the rail. clean monotone sweep, broad peak 0.003-0.004; baked 0.003 -> +1.9pp full scale (56.2->58.1%), residual collapsed t=-26.5->-1.5, model ece 0.0060 (better than market's 0.0069). sanity check: 0.003/lane => draw-14 vs draw-1 runs ~3.9% (~62m) longer over 1600m -- the right order for the extra arc of being ~13 lanes wider round the turns, so the calibrated magnitude lands in the geometric ballpark (physical, not a fudge). interaction (per user: draw is a proxy for geometry and collision -- horses are not collisionless, the abm's original motivation): the residual has a field-size gradient (small fields over-penalised, crowded under) -- the collision fingerprint. but a mean-field field-size modulation (draw_fs_gain, wired+unbaked) recovers only ~0.1pp; the full draw x crowding / boxed-in / draw x pace structure is genuinely the agent-based sim's job (place/exotics). lesson: a 'parked / low-leverage' verdict can go stale when the production sim changes -- always re-check parked items against the current production path. bodywt (t=+9.6) is the next such re-check.
